programme.title: Trusadh (Compelling Stories)
programme.desc: Following a year in the life of student and Gaelic learner Loretta Crinall, as she leaves her home in Glasgow and makes her way to the largest city in South America, Sao Paulo, as part of her languages degree. Having recently left her career as a drag performer, Loretta is now embarking on a journey to an unknown country with all the challenges that come with it. As a minority language scholar and activist, this trip gives her the opportunity to conduct in-depth research on the regions indigenous people. On the Jaragua Mountain, on the outskirts of Sao Paulo, she meets the Guarani people who have lived there for centuries. In a conversation with Anthony Karai Poty, Loretta hears how the Guarani have fought to defend their way of life against violence and ignorance. This journey also gives Loretta the opportunity to look back on her life growing up as a black, trans woman, and the impact that has had on her, both personally and politically

Featuring contributions from musical collaborators Eilidh Cormack, Lana Pheutan and Ruairidh Gray, with highlights from their sell-out show at the Glasgow Barrowlands

programme.title: Coin Trusaidh/Muster Dogs
programme.desc: An intimate character journey about the lives of five very different Australian dog trainers as they participate in an experiment to take a new Kelpie pup and transform it from a greenhorn to an efficient working member of the mustering pack. These cute new puppies instantly wriggle their way into the hearts of our new owners and training begins quickly. Names are given and Annie, Gossip, Lucifer, Spice and Chet embark on the challenge of training for the first assessment of their skills at four months

programme.title: Srb: Scotland on Coffee
programme.desc: Ellen MacDonald embarks on a journey to discover all there is to know about coffee. Her adventure takes her to a coffee farm in Kenya, where she learns about the hard work behind growing coffee beans. Back in Scotland, she visits local roasteries and attends the lively Glasgow Coffee Festival, all while training with one of the country's best baristas as she explores coffee culture in Scotland

programme.desc: The traditional French bistro is mounting a comeback. In recent times, an average of 25 a day have been shutting their doors, as eating habits change across France. programme.title: Rikki
programme.desc: Ashley Jensen narrates a programme celebrating the life, career and legacy of Rikki Fulton, one of Scotland's most beloved comic actors and undisputed King of Hogmanay. programme.desc: Trent Rockets Women v Birmingham Phoenix Women (Start-time 3.00pm). Coverage of the match from Trent Bridge in Nottingham. The Phoenix won the toss and elected to bat when these teams faced each other at Edgbaston last year, and went on to post a total of 148/5 from their 100 balls, which proved to be enough for victory as the Rockets fell 11 runs short in their innings, despite Nat Sciver-Brunt scoring 64 from 40 deliveries

programme.title: The Hundred Live
programme.desc: Trent Rockets Men v Birmingham Phoenix Men (Start-time 6.30pm). Coverage of the match from Trent Bridge in Nottingham. The Rockets claimed a six-wicket victory when these teams clashed at Edgbaston last season, thanks largely to the efforts of fast bowler Lockie Ferguson who three wickets with his 20 balls and helped restrict the Phoenix to 122/6, which the Rockets surpassed with 22 balls to spare

programme.desc: The Washington DC Open. Coverage of day five of the WTA 500 and ATP 500 event, a hard-court tournament held at William H.G. FitzGerald Tennis Center in the USA. All four the women's quarter-finals 12 months ago were settled in straight sets, with notable wins for 2021 US Open champion Emma Raducanu, who beat Maria Sakkari 6-4 7-5, while the woman she beat in that memorable final, Leylah Fernandez, triumphed 6-4 7-6 over Taylor Townsend. Four of the eight men's quarter-finalists last year were American, but only one of them progressed to the semi-finals, with Ben Shelton winning 7-6 6-4 against his compatriot Frances Tiafoe

Today will see the conclusion of the first round in both competitions, with players hoping to avoid elimination at the first step. Jacob Fearnley was the only British male involved at this stage last year, and suffered an early exit following a 2-6 3-6 loss to Argentinean qualifier Juan Pablo Ficovich. There were mixed fortunes for British representation in the women's competition, with Emma Raducanu booking her place in round two with a 6-2 6-4 win over Elena-Gabriela Ruse, but Katie Boulter was knocked out at the first time of asking as she lost 1-6 5-7 to Renata Zaraza
